newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shekel weakens against dollar, basket.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shekel weakens against dollar, basket.

text.p: The Israeli shekel weakened slightly against the dollar and the basket of foreign currencies recovering from early losses due to a lower-than-expected September inflation figure, dealers said.

"The shekel began falling (late) Tuesday after the release of the lower-than-expected consumer price index," said a dealer at United Mizrahi Bank. "The trend continued today mainly due to active inter-bank trading."

Hopes that the Bank of Israel would make a significant reduction in short-term rates grew on Tuesday with the news of a low 0.4 percent rise in the September consumer price index. The CPI was announced after the Tuesday representative rate was fixed.

"When the dollar reached 3.2150 shekels (today) the business sector started selling dollars and the shekel recovered," the dealer said. "The Bank of Israel was not active in the market, and in late afternoon the basket was trading 6.85 percent below the mid-point."

The shekel is allowed to trade in a band of seven percent above or below a sloping midpoint designed to devalue the Israeli currency by six percent a year against a basket of currencies representing Israel's main trading partners.

The representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.2030 against 3.1970 on Tuesday. The basket, composed of the dollar, mark, pound sterling, French franc and yen, closed at 3.5712 shekels against 3.5648 on Tuesday.
On the crosses the shekel traded against the yen at 2.8551 shekels per 100 yen against 2.8467 on Tuesday and against the mark at 2.0790 shekels against 2.0772 on Tuesday.
In late afternoon the dollar was trading at 3.2005 shekels.
